title: Overtime, commission and piecework
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:20Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point covers the new point's full idea: mat-commission-piecework covers commission and piecework but not overtime, and mat-overtime-penalty-rates covers overtime and penalty rates but not commission or piecework, so no single bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Overtime, commission and piecework
card: Hours worked beyond normal hours are paid at a higher rate. Time-and-a-half means \(1.5 \times\) the normal hourly rate. Double time means \(2 \times\) the normal rate.
A worker earns a percentage of the value of what they sell. Commission \(=\) rate \(\times\) sales.
A worker is paid a set amount for each item made. Pay \(=\) rate per item \(\times\) number of items.
Ravi earns $20 an hour. Three hours of time-and-a-half pays \(3 \times 1.5 \times 20 = 90\) dollars.
draft.remember: Overtime raises the hourly rate, commission follows sales, and piecework follows items made.

a.q: Mei earns $18 an hour. How much is she paid for 4 hours of overtime at time-and-a-half?
a.why: Time-and-a-half is \(1.5 \times 18 = 27\) dollars an hour. For 4 hours, \(4 \times 27 = 108\) dollars. $72 is wrong because it uses the normal rate and leaves out the extra half.
a.clue: Find the overtime hourly rate first.

b.q: Tom sells cars in Orange and earns 3% commission on sales. He sells cars worth $85,000 in a week. What is his commission?
b.why: Commission is \(0.03 \times 85\,000 = 2550\) dollars. $255 is wrong because it uses 0.3% instead of 3%, a slip when changing a percentage to a decimal.
b.clue: Change 3% to a decimal, then multiply by the sales.
